name: Vedic Peoples
place: the Punjab and the Ganges plain
desc: Herders of cattle and horses who sang the hymns of the Rigveda around their fire altars and passed them down, word for word, by memory alone for three thousand years. Their descendants cleared the Ganges forests with iron, founded the kingdoms of Magadha, and gave birth to the Upanishads, the Buddha and Mahavira.
source: The Rigveda and later Vedic texts, preserved by oral recitation; the Sulba Sutras; archaeology of the Painted Grey Ware culture

devout: recited a whole book of hymns without missing a syllable
belligerent: drove a chariot across the river in the cattle raid
gluttonous: brought the herd home from the far pastures with every calf

inventions.name: Perfect Recitation
inventions.source: Vedic chant was preserved by methods of recitation (word by word, in pairs, back and forth) so exact that the Rigveda survives unchanged; UNESCO lists it as world heritage
inventions.desc: Hymns learned forwards, backwards and in pairs, so not a syllable is ever lost: the tribe gathers more lore, rites bring 5% more devotion.
inventions.hint: Comes from long rites and nights at the fire.

inventions.name: Geometry of the Cords
inventions.source: The Sulba Sutras (c. 800–500 BCE) give rules for building fire altars with cords and pegs, including the theorem later named after Pythagoras
inventions.desc: Squares, circles and right angles laid out with knotted cords for the fire altars: building is 10% faster, a little more lore.
inventions.hint: Needs the Tribe & Agrarian Era, and builders who keep the rites.

inventions.name: Iron Ploughshare
inventions.source: Iron tools spread through the Ganges plain from about 1000 BCE, opening its forests to rice farming
inventions.desc: An iron tip for the plough and an iron axe for the jungle: farm plots yield 20% more, woodcutting 10% faster.

inventions.name: Herbs of the Atharvaveda
inventions.source: The Atharvaveda contains charms and herbal cures that are the roots of later Ayurveda
inventions.desc: Roots and leaves given with a chant for each sickness: the sick recover 20% faster, the hurt heal 5% faster.

foods.name: Rice with Ghee
foods.desc: Rice from the wet fields, boiled and eaten with melted butter: hunger grows 10% slower.
foods.hint: Needs wild rice and Beast Domestication.

foods.name: Madhuparka
foods.source: Vedic custom offered an honoured guest madhuparka, a mixture of curd, honey and ghee
foods.desc: Curd, honey and ghee stirred together for every guest: +3 mood.

finds.name: Wild Rice
finds.source: Rice was gathered and then farmed in the Ganges valley (Lahuradewa) from very early times
finds.desc: Grass of the wet margins, its grains falling at a touch. Gathering it brings farming closer.

finds.name: Turmeric
finds.desc: A golden root for colour, flavour and healing wounds.

people.name: Vishvara
people.desc: He knows ten thousand verses and never misses one.
memory: sang the hymn to Agni at dawn as his grandfather taught him

people.name: Gavaksha
people.desc: In this tribe wealth is counted in cows, and she has the most.
memory: found the stolen cattle in a cave and brought them home

people.name: Ghosha
people.source: Two hymns of the Rigveda (10.39–40) are attributed to her
people.desc: A woman seer who, the hymns say, was healed of a skin disease by the twin horsemen of the gods, and married late and happily.

people.name: Panini
people.source: The Ashtadhyayi, about 4,000 rules describing Sanskrit, c. 4th century BCE
people.desc: A scholar of Gandhara who described a whole language in four thousand short rules, a feat linguists still admire.

people.name: Jivaka
people.source: Buddhist texts: a foundling raised at the court of Magadha who studied medicine at Taxila and became physician to the Buddha
people.text: a young doctor back from the great school in the north-west, who says every plant within a day's walk is a medicine.
memory: searched a whole day's walk around Taxila and found no plant that was not a medicine
people.desc: In legend, the greatest physician of the Buddha's time.

people.name: Sudas
people.label: Sudas, Victor of the Ten Kings
people.desc: A king who beats ten kings at the river. Combat 8.

people.name: Yajnavalkya
people.label: Yajnavalkya the Sage
people.desc: He wins every debate and walks away from his riches. Lore 9.

people.name: Gargi
people.label: Gargi, who Questioned the Sage
people.desc: A woman philosopher who asks what the world is woven on. Lore 8, Crafting 4.

events.title: Ten Kings at the River
events.source: Rigveda 7.18: King Sudas of the Bharatas defeated a confederacy of ten tribes on the Parushni river
events.text: Ten neighbouring clans have joined together against us and are coming across the river. The singers say the gods are with us; the war leaders want to break the dykes and let the river fight for us.

options.label: Break the dykes

do.remember: broke the dykes when the ten kings crossed the river

options.result: The river rises under the enemy. The ten kings' army is swept away, and the singers make a new hymn.

options.label: Offer cattle for peace
options.result: Cattle cross the river instead of warriors.

events.title: The Horse Goes Free
events.source: The ashvamedha: a consecrated horse wandered for a year, followed by warriors; every land it crossed had to accept the king or fight
events.text: The priests propose the great horse rite: a white stallion set free to wander for a year, followed by our warriors. Every land it walks through will be ours, or will fight.

options.label: Let the horse go
options.result: A year later the horse comes home, and many chiefs have bowed rather than fight.

options.label: Too proud a rite
options.result: The horse stays in its stall.

events.title: A Thousand Cows for the Wisest
events.source: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 3: King Janaka offered a thousand cows with gold on their horns to the wisest sage at his court
events.text: The chief offers a hundred cows to whoever can answer every question about the world. The wise ones gather, and the debate lasts three days.

do.remember: debated for three days about what the world is woven on

tales.name: Indra Frees the Waters
tales.text: The serpent Vritra lay coiled around the mountain and held back all the waters of the world. Indra drank the soma, took up the thunderbolt the craftsman had made him, and struck the serpent down. The waters rushed out like lowing cows running to their calves, and the rivers flowed to the sea.
tales.moral: what is held back must be set free

tales.name: Manu and the Fish
tales.text: As Manu washed his hands, a little fish came into them and said: keep me, and I will save you. He kept it in a jar, then a pond, then the sea, as it grew. One day it said: a flood is coming; build a boat. When the waters rose, the fish towed the boat to a mountain in the north, and Manu alone was saved.
tales.moral: kindness to the small is repaid

tales.name: Nachiketa and Death
tales.text: A boy, given to Death by his angry father, waited three days at Death's door with nothing to eat. Death, ashamed, offered him three wishes. The boy asked for his father's peace, for the secret of the fire, and for the answer to one question: what happens after we die? Death offered him gold and kingdoms instead, but the boy would not be put off.

tales.name: The Hymn to Dawn
tales.source: Rigveda hymns to Ushas, goddess of dawn
tales.text: She comes like a young woman shining, waking every living thing, driving away the black cloak of night. She has shone before; she will shine after. She sets the birds flying from their nests and the people to their work. Shine on us today, Dawn, with wealth of cattle and of children.
